## Investigative objective

The goal of this project is to conduct two independent data analysis using two distinct datasets investigated in class, and producing two vignettes.

The first dataset will be the `waterborne` dataset in the `finalproject` package. The aim is to conduct analysis on the geographic trends of waterborne diseases outbreaks in the United States, and explore which pathogen has the greatest impact.

The second dataset will be the `NHANES` dataset in the `NHANES` package. The aim is to investigate the distribution of health indicators (such as BMI and blood pressure) across different groups (such as age and gender).

## Datasets

`waterborne`

- Source: Data on waterborne disease provided by the US CDC.

- Variables of Interest: state, etiology, illnesses, deaths, water exposure, water types

`NHANES`

- Source: The National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey conducted by the US CDC.

- Variables of interest: age, sex, race, education, BMI, systolic blood pressure, diabetes.

## Plans

For `waterborne`: Calculation of outbreak frequencies by etiology and state, and create plots to visualize trend of disease outbreaks over years. Focus on the epidemiological trend and characteristics of outbreaks.

For `NHANES` : Explore associations between variables, doing tests. Doing visualization to compare between population subgroups.

## Limitations

The `waterborne` dataset depend on the voluntary reports of local health departments, which will likely underestimate the true burden of the waterborne diseases. The `NHANES` dataset is cross-sectional, so a causal relationship cannot be derived from the data. Moreover, this dataset depend highly on self-reported information.
